rubrics.intent_basis: Single-item reads and membership queries use only the driver operations needed by those paths.

rubrics.criterion: Single-item read clients depend on a read-specific capability boundary instead of the entire driver session.
rubrics.acceptance: Trace hasItem and getItem through mount selection and find that unrelated mutation and lifecycle capabilities are not required to satisfy their internal contract. Keep public Driver optional shape unchanged; shared concrete session is legal behind focused read contract. Mount lookup returns source identity via getMount/getMounts. Shared implementations and coherent combined contracts are valid; only actual client requirements must narrow. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Renaming DriverSession or moving all its members to a different file leaves these readers coupled to it.

rubrics.intent_basis: Ordinary and raw writes have optional driver methods and synthetic update notifications when native watch is absent.
rubrics.baseline_defect: Both setItem and setItemRaw plus mutation notification defaults live in the same mandatory session used by readers and overlay enumeration.
rubrics.criterion: Write capability checks, raw fallback, and update notification form a write-focused boundary that is not a required dependency of read-only consumers.
rubrics.acceptance: Follow ordinary and raw writes through native/fallback paths and see their mutation-specific dependency without carrying the complete session contract into readers. Readonly setItem returns before stringify; undefined delegates remove with existing options behavior; source presence checked dynamically, not inferred from mandatory adapter method. rubrics.intent_basis: A raw write without native setItemRaw falls through the ordinary writer; the existing storage API has one update event per successful logical write.
rubrics.baseline_defect: The session now routes raw fallback through session.setItem with a per-call Mutation callback, mixing encoding, capability dispatch, and event policy in the broad adapter.
rubrics.criterion: Raw fallback and ordinary-write event policy have a coherent mutation owner that emits one logical update and does not impose callback policy on unrelated capabilities.
rubrics.acceptance: A native raw writer and the serializeRaw-to-setItem path each reach one write-specific event decision after completion; the broad read/list/watch contract is not needed to implement it. After successful native raw write or serialized ordinary fallback, check CURRENT watch availability then exactly one synthetic update; never precheck watch or duplicate fallback event. Scoped helper may implement both ordinary/raw. Shared implementations and coherent combined contracts are valid; only actual client requirements must narrow. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Adding a second notification in storage.setItemRaw while retaining the session callback, or passing callbacks through a renamed global adapter, does not meet the boundary.

rubrics.intent_basis: removeItem may delete the metadata companion key and then issue one remove event for the requested item.
rubrics.baseline_defect: The broad session's removeItem now recursively removes the companion key while accepting notification policy and a removeMeta flag from storage.
rubrics.criterion: Item removal and optional metadata cleanup are owned by a focused mutation path that keeps the companion operation subordinate to the logical removal.
rubrics.acceptance: The caller's legacy removeMeta/removeMata interpretation, companion-key deletion, and one parent notification can be traced without requiring read/batch/overlay clients to depend on removal policy. Remove main then key+$ only for removeMeta/removeMata, child receives no mutation context; only parent event after both success. Failure suppresses event; absent remove remains readonly. Shared implementations and coherent combined contracts are valid; only actual client requirements must narrow. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Renaming the recursive method or emitting a separate child notification leaves the broad ownership or logical removal defect unresolved.

rubrics.intent_basis: Mount selection produces a relative key and base, and storage watchers consume a full-key change event.
rubrics.baseline_defect: A WeakMap-cached session is shared by driver identity while storage passes a per-operation closure that adds the selected mount base to session-emitted relative keys.
rubrics.criterion: The mount producer, mutation boundary, and watcher consumer coordinate key attribution without storing a mount-specific base on a shared driver capability object.
rubrics.acceptance: When one driver is mounted under two bases, each logical update/remove reaches onChange with its own full key through a scoped handoff; the capability split retains that relation. WeakMap caches per Driver, so capture mount base per call rather than mutable session-global base. Equivalent design without cache valid; watch callback adds its own mount prefix exactly once. Shared implementations and coherent combined contracts are valid; only actual client requirements must narrow. Equivalent functions, policy data, composition or a redesigned flow qualify; no prescribed helper, class, file, return object or one-component-per-item design is required. One coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Putting base on the cached session can attribute both mounts' events to the wrong path even if tests pass for one mount.

rubrics.intent_basis: Metadata reads combine optional native metadata with the separate stored `$` value when nativeOnly is false.

rubrics.acceptance: Trace getMeta to native and custom sources and see their merge at a focused owner while non-metadata operations avoid the metadata contract. Native meta first then custom key+$ unless nativeOnly; null-prototype result, custom overwrites native; string atime/mtime become Dates. Current method/source capabilities and async order preserved. rubrics.intent_basis: Mounted drivers already vary in native clear support; fallback enumerates and removes keys when clear is absent.

rubrics.acceptance: Both current clear alternatives remain available, and the internal contract needed for hasItem/getItem does not include clear or its fallback dependencies. Native clear uses detached adapter call; fallback getKeys/removeItem retain source receiver-bound calls, base||empty and concurrent removal; absent remover readonly, no invented per-item synthetic notifications. rubrics.intent_basis: Watch subscriptions and disposal occur on storage start/stop, mount/unmount, and overlay layer cleanup.

rubrics.intent_basis: Overlay hasItem/getItem read ordered layers and interpret a top-layer tombstone.
rubrics.baseline_defect: src/drivers/overlay.ts constructs full receiver-bound DriverSession objects for layer reads, which import the same mutation, metadata, clear, watch and disposal surface used by storage.

rubrics.acceptance: The producer of layer capabilities and overlay's hasItem/getItem can be traced through ordered layers and tombstone checks without requiring unrelated session methods. rubrics.intent_basis: Overlay writes and tombstone removal target the first layer, whereas key enumeration reads all layers and masks tombstoned keys.
